title: Spark failures and recovery
hypothesis: Spark's task retries absorb an executor loss; the playbook fixes out-of-memory within 2 retries; adaptive execution handles skew.
conclusion: Reference clean run: 8078 rows, content hash 1d1ca664a2174556. low_driver_memory: recovered=False in 2 attempt(s) (1 retries, 276.2s), remedies [], output identical to the clean run: False. sandbox_container_killed: recovered=True in 1 attempt(s) (0 retries, 170.4s), remedies [], output identical to the clean run: False. skewed_one_customer_20pct: recovered=True in 1 attempt(s) (0 retries, 87.4s), remedies [], output identical to the clean run: None. 2 of 3 injected faults recovered. The executor kill landed on a real container: False. The out-of-memory arm is the one that matters most here: it is the test that RAISE_EXECUTOR_MEMORY reaches the submitted job at all, which it did not until this experiment was written - the retry used to be given exactly the memory that had just failed.
limitations: Spark runs in local mode inside the sandbox, so the driver is the executor. Killing the sandbox container is therefore losing the executor, which is the closest this environment reaches to the PRD's distributed executor loss - not a measurement of a multi-executor cluster shedding one worker (ADR-0002).

The container kill did not land: no sandbox container was seen while the job ran, so that arm measures an ordinary run and not a recovery. FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'docker'
